t:
(a) In General.—Section 8415(f) of title 5, United States Code, is amended to read as follows:“(f) The annuity of an air traffic controller or former air traffic controller retiring under section 8412(a) is computed under subsection (a), except that if the individual has at least 5 years of service in any combination as—“(1) an air traffic controller as defined by section 2109(1)(A)(i);“(2) a first level supervisor of an air traffic controller as defined by section 2109(1)(A)(i); or“(3) a second level supervisor of an air traffic controller as defined by section 2109(1)(A)(i);so much of the annuity as is computed with respect to such type of service shall be computed by multiplying 1 7/10 percent of the individual’s average pay by the years of such service.”. 
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendment made by subsection (a) shall be deemed to be effective on December 12, 2003. 
    (c) Procedures Required.—The Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall establish such procedures as are necessary to provide for—
        (1) notification to each annuitant affected by the amendments made by this section; 
        (2) recalculation of the benefits of affected annuitants; 
        (3) an adjustment to applicable monthly benefit amounts pursuant to such recalculation, to begin as soon as is practicable; and 
        (4) a lump-sum payment to each affected annuitant equal to the additional total benefit amount that such annuitant would have received had the amendment made by subsection (a) been in effect on December 12, 2003.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that "establish such procedures" amounts to rulemaking, or that notifying annuitants is participation. The section does not call for regulations, comment, hearings, or consultation with any outside party; the procedures are internal administrative steps for recalculating and paying benefits. Notification to annuitants is one-way notice of a benefit adjustment, not input into a federal decision.

opus.w: The section changes how air traffic controllers' annuities are calculated and tells OPM to set up internal procedures to notify affected annuitants, recalculate their benefits and pay them. Notifying annuitants of a change Congress has already made is one-way communication, not consulting outsiders before a decision. Nothing here calls for regulations, a comment period, a hearing, an advisory body or a right to sue. Reading 'establish procedures' as rulemaking stretches the text, because it describes administrative steps, not a grant of authority to regulate.

opus.b: I'm labelling this **No**. One reading is tempting but wrong: the Director of OPM must "establish such procedures," which could look like rulemaking (Example 6 counted authority to act "by regulation" as participation), and the procedures include "notification" to annuitants, who are outside the government. That reading fails. The section never calls for regulations or a comment period. The notice to annuitants only goes one way, telling them about a benefit change that has already been decided. Recalculating benefits and making payments are benefit administration, not outside input into a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section outlines administrative procedures for calculating and paying federal employee retirement benefits. The definition explicitly states that participation does not include applications for benefits or grants. Since this text concerns the internal processing and distribution of benefits to federal employees, it does not involve outside parties participating in a federal decision.
qwen_chat.s: (c) Procedures Required.—The Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall establish such procedures as are necessary to provide for— (1) notification to each annuitant affected by the amendments made by this section; (2) recalculation of the benefits of affected annuitants; (3) an adjustment to applicable monthly benefit amounts pursuant to such recalculation, to begin as soon as is practicable; and (4) a lump-sum payment to each affected annuitant equal to the additional total benefit amount that such annuitant would have received had the amendment made by subsection (a) been in effect on December 12, 2003.
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it involves notifying annuitants and recalculating their benefits.
Resolution: This is an administrative process for calculating and paying federal employee retirement benefits. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and this section deals with the internal calculation and distribution of those benefits, not with outside parties participating in a decision-making process.
